summary: [¶] - (f) J&K SLDC persistently defaults on the payment of Deviation Charges and legacy dues. Furthermore, JKSLDC did not open the requisite Letters of Credit (LC) against the said default, thereby violating Regulation 10.1 and Regulation 10.2 of the DSM Regulations respectively. [¶] - (k) The adverse fallout of the non-payment of Deviation Charges by the JKPCL affects the grid operations in the form of an increase in grid indiscipline. Also, after the implementation of the CERC (Ancillary Services Operations) Regulations, payment to ancillary service & SCUC providers must be made from the pool balance of the Regional Deviation Pool Account Fund. Non-payment by pool members is creating a deficit in the Regional Deviation Pool Account Fund and affecting disbursements to receivable entities, ancillary service providers, and SCUC providers. Any regular default by the pool members in the Regional Deviation Pool Account Fund also affects the settlement of Ancillary Services, thereby creating serious concerns for grid discipline and monitoring. [para 9] 9. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner reiterated that there was a persistent default by the Respondents in the payment of the deviation charges, including the legacy dues, under the DSM Regulations and hence the present petition was filed. In response, counsel for the Respondent pointed out that a lump-sum amount of Rs. 30 crore was paid to the Petitioner towards deviation charges, but, due to financial constraints, the Respondent may be granted a six-month extension of time to clear the balance dues. Accordingly, the Commission directed the Petitioner to respond to the Respondent's specific prayer for a six-month extension of time for payment of the balance dues in the rejoinder affidavit. [¶] - (a) In response to the specific prayer of the Respondent, JKPCL, during the hearing held on 27.10.2025, the Commission, if it deems fit, may grant a total period of six months to JKPCL for liquidation of all outstanding dues, including DSM Charges, Legacy Pool Deficit Recovery Charges, and Current Pool Deficit Recovery Charges and may accordingly issue necessary directions as suggested below: [para 13] 13. Brief facts of the case: The Petitioner, NRLDC, filed the present petition under Section 79 and Section 142 of the Electricity Act 2003 against JKPCL and JKSLDC for persistent default in payment of deviation charges, DSM Pool Deficit Recovery Charges and related dues under the DSM Regulations, 2024. Petitioner submitted that the last payment of Rs. 20.22 crore was received into the pool from JKPCL on 09.02.2024 towards the outstanding dues, and thereafter, no further payments were received. The deviation charges payable by JKPCL to the “Northern Regional Pool Account” piled up and stand at around Rs. 114.06 crore as on 28.02.2025 (principal amount). Further, in line with the DSM Regulations, 2024 and the NLDC letter dated 11.11.2024 regarding the payment of Net Deviation & Ancillary Services Pool Account Deficit Recovery for the period before 16.09.2024 (Statement of Legacy Dues), the total outstanding legacy dues amount to Rs.44.99 crore. The Petitioner submitted that JKSLDC did not open the requisite Letters of Credit (LCs) against the said default, thereby violating Regulations 10.1 and 10.2 of the DSM Regulations and seeks intervention from the Commission regarding the difficulties encountered in discharging its statutory functions under the DSM Regulations, 2024.
